# Leafnote: product definition

This file is the only source of truth for anything an article says about the product. If a feature isn't listed under "What exists", treat it as not existing. When in doubt, leave it out or ask the owner.

## Identity

- **Name:** Leafnote
- **What it is:** A watering reminder app for houseplants
- **Type:** app
- **Who it's for:** People with 5 to 50 houseplants who keep forgetting which plant needs water
- **Official links (the only URLs to use for the product):**
  - Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=example.leafnote
- **Pricing (say exactly this, nothing more):** Free to download, with an optional Plus subscription. Never state a price.

## What exists

- **Per-plant watering schedules** _(Free)_: Each plant gets its own interval in days; the app reminds you on the day it's due.
- **Snooze and skip** _(Free)_: Push a reminder by one to three days, or skip it if the soil is still wet.
- **Watering log** _(Free)_: Every watering is logged with the date, so you can see the real interval over time.
- **Seasonal adjustment** _(Plus)_: Lengthen all intervals by a percentage for winter with one setting.
- **CSV export** _(Plus)_: Export the watering log as a CSV file.

## What does NOT exist (never claim or imply these)

- No plant identification from photos
- No disease or pest diagnosis
- No soil moisture sensor support
- No iPhone version (Android only)
- No sharing with other household members
- Anything about user numbers, ratings, reviews, awards, press or "trusted by": not provided unless listed above. Don't state or imply any.

## How to talk about it

Leafnote fits someone with enough plants that a calendar gets messy. Someone with three plants is fine with a phone calendar; someone who wants plant ID or diagnosis needs a different app.

- Disclosure line for lists and comparisons: "Full disclosure: we make Leafnote."
- Don't promise plants will survive or thrive
- No timing claims like 'set up in 30 seconds'
- One product section and one CTA per article is enough. Say plainly when another tool or a spreadsheet fits a reader better.
